steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Context: The Elizabethan era saw a significant expansion in education, driven by the Renaissance emphasis on learning and the growing need for educated administrators, lawyers, and clergy. However, education was still limited by class and gender: most children received no formal education, and opportunities for girls were extremely restricted. | The Purpose of Education: Education in Elizabethan England was not about developing the individual - it was about producing trained men who could serve the state as administrators, diplomats, lawyers, and clergy. A knowledge of Latin was essential for all official and academic communication.
